TERMS OF SERVICE

Clear terms for working with Cyberfreak Software.

These terms explain the general basis on which Cyberfreak Software Limited provides services and uses this website.

Last updated: 17 November 2026

These terms apply to the Cyberfreak Software website and, unless a separate written agreement says otherwise, provide the general framework for enquiries and services supplied by Cyberfreak Software Limited (“CFS”, “we”, “us” or “our”). They are written to make the working relationship clear and practical. A proposal, order confirmation or separate agreement may set out the particular service, price, timing and scope agreed with a customer; where it does, that document takes precedence over these general terms to the extent of any conflict.

Using this website

We aim to keep the information on this website accurate and useful, but it is general information rather than advice tailored to a particular business, website or technical environment. You may use the site for legitimate business enquiries and to learn about our services. You must not interfere with the site, attempt to access areas that are not intended for public access, introduce harmful code or use the site in a way that is unlawful or disrupts other users.

The site may link to third-party websites or services, including portfolio projects and social-media platforms. Those links are provided for convenience and do not mean that CFS controls, approves or accepts responsibility for the third-party site, its availability or its content.

Enquiries, proposals and agreed work

An enquiry through our contact form does not create a contract or commit either party to work. Before work begins, we will normally discuss the required outcome, the information or access needed, the scope of the service and the commercial arrangements. We may decline work that does not fit our availability, expertise or the intended use of a service.

Customers are responsible for supplying accurate information, holding the permissions needed to give us access to relevant websites, accounts or material, and making timely decisions where their input is needed. If a request materially changes after work has begun, we will discuss whether it changes the scope, timing or price before proceeding.

Fees and payment

Fees, billing frequency, payment method, commencement date and any cancellation arrangements are confirmed in the applicable proposal, order confirmation or service agreement. Unless expressly agreed otherwise, work that falls outside an agreed scope is not included merely because it is related to the same website or business objective. We will raise additional work for discussion before undertaking it.

Website deployments and software work

Website deployments, software projects and technical support vary substantially between customers. The relevant proposal or project agreement should therefore identify the deliverables, acceptance approach, access required, third-party services involved and any ongoing support arrangements. Customers remain responsible for the accuracy, legality and rights clearance of the material they provide or ask us to publish, unless we have expressly agreed another arrangement.

SEO Management service terms

What the standard service includes

CFS provides ongoing search engine optimisation monitoring and management services as agreed with each customer. The standard service can include Google Search Console configuration and monitoring, sitemap-related management, analysis of organic search performance, identification of keyword opportunities and periodic performance reporting. The precise scope is confirmed before the service begins, because the appropriate setup depends on the website, its platform and the access available.

We may set up or obtain suitable access to a Google Search Console property, check sitemap configuration, submit a sitemap to Google and monitor organic search clicks, impressions and indexed pages. We may examine performance over time, analyse the search queries associated with a website and provide clear monthly reporting with practical keyword or content recommendations.

Access and limited technical configuration

Customers agree to provide the permissions and access reasonably necessary to deliver the agreed service. This may include Google Search Console permissions, website administration access, hosting information, domain-verification access or other relevant technical access. Where needed, CFS may carry out limited technical configuration connected with sitemap management, Search Console verification or the agreed monitoring setup. This can include lightweight changes such as adding a verification meta tag or configuring automatic sitemap generation where technically feasible.

Material website changes outside that monitoring and configuration scope require separate discussion and authorisation. Customers should maintain appropriate website backups and notify us of significant website, domain, hosting or platform changes that could affect monitoring.

What is not included in the monthly subscription

The standard SEO Management subscription does not include website content creation, article writing, creating new website pages, bespoke web development, website redesign or substantial technical remediation unless separately agreed. CFS may recommend these activities where useful, but recommendations are not an instruction or a commitment for CFS to implement them within the subscription. A customer may arrange recommended work with its existing developer or content provider, or ask CFS to quote separately where appropriate.

Search performance and keyword recommendations

Search rankings, indexing decisions and organic search traffic are influenced by factors outside CFS’s direct control. CFS does not guarantee that Google will index a particular page or that particular rankings, traffic volumes, enquiries, leads or sales will be achieved. Keyword opportunities are recommendations based on available data, not guarantees of future ranking or traffic improvement.

Reports reflect information available from Google Search Console and other expressly agreed data sources. Such data may be incomplete, delayed or revised by its provider. Where a property has limited history or insufficient data, a report may explain that monitoring remains in progress rather than present unsupported conclusions.

Monthly reporting

Customers will ordinarily receive a monthly SEO performance report for the applicable reporting period. Depending on the information available, it may cover clicks, impressions, indexed-page information, comparisons with earlier periods and relevant keyword opportunities. The report is intended to make search performance understandable and support sensible future decisions; it is not a guarantee of a particular business outcome.

Intellectual property and confidentiality

Each party keeps ownership of material it owned before the engagement. Unless an agreed project document says otherwise, CFS retains ownership of its pre-existing tools, methods, templates and know-how. We will use customer information only as reasonably necessary to provide the agreed service and to meet legal obligations. Customers should avoid sending passwords through ordinary email or a contact form; secure access should be arranged through an appropriate method.

Liability and service availability

We take reasonable care in providing our services, but websites, search platforms, hosting services and other third-party systems can change or fail without warning. Nothing on this site excludes or limits liability that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited. Any additional liability, warranty, service-level or remedy arrangements should be recorded in the agreement for the relevant service.

Privacy and changes to these terms

Our Privacy Policy explains how we handle personal information. We may update these terms when our services, website or legal obligations change. The version published here applies to use of this website from its publication date; a customer’s separately agreed service terms are not changed retrospectively without discussion.
